findings.reason: the plan exists to fix a loaded node's session start, and without a loaded-condition arm the node can satisfy its gate while the reported symptom still occurs.
findings.text: the gate measures "the median of five cold starts on a debug-partition node" while §1 measured the failure at load average 73 on the fleet node; the done-when records the node's load but requires no comparable load, so a pass on a quiet node cannot show that a session on a loaded node now answers inside the client's 30 s limit

findings.reason: the done-when's whole content is a recorded measurement, and a later reader cannot open a measurement that has no path; other plans in this repository carry theirs under `docs/evidence/<topic>/`.
findings.text: nothing in the plan names a durable location for the five cold-start timings, the node's load, the base-revision measurements or the base failure the negative control is shown at, so the evidence the gate rests on survives only inside one run's manifest

findings.reason: the profile the plan cites accounts for 19.9 s of 27.5 s and therefore does not show that cutting those imports meets a 5 s target; stating the residual's composition, or measuring it, is what makes the target checkable rather than a guess a node may miss for an unrelated reason.
findings.text: the cited numbers leave 7.6 s of the 27.5 s `--help` wall time outside the 19.9 s import profile, while §2 asks `imas-codex serve --help` to return in under 5 s; spawn overhead measured on this node is 0.84–1.32 s (`uv run --no-sync --project . python -c pass`) against 0.23 s for the interpreter alone, so the residual is not process spawn and the plan never says what it is made of; the section names no measure of it

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `.mcp.json` exists and spawns `imas-codex serve` through `uv run --no-sync --project`, `imas_codex/cli/serve.py` carries the `--read-only` and `--dd-only` options that make three serve modes real, and the plan file itself resolves in `docs/plans/`.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's timing gate measures on a debug-partition node at whatever load it happens to carry, while §1 measures the defect at load average 73.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: a finding — §2 requires five timings, the node's load, the base-revision arms and the negative control's base failure recorded, and no durable path is named anywhere in the plan.
rubric_items.naming: pass — no symbol, filename or comment is named, so nothing carries a plan label, stage name or ticket identifier, and the prose states mechanisms ("the server command pays for every other command's imports") rather than changelog.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the plan's own decomposition leaves 7.6 s of the 27.5 s `--help` wall time unattributed and §2 targets under 5 s, so the cited profile does not show the target is reachable; the root-cause claim itself (imports dominate: 19.9 s of 27.5 s) does match the cited profile, and no section prescribes an implementation.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one deliverable, cutting the server's start-up cost, with the tool-list and command-list checks reading as regression guards rather than second goals.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — the plan is standalone as declared, sprint S19 carries it, no other plan references its slug, and both sections' data-status match plan-section-declarations.
